title: Senior Associate, Analytics
description:
About WPP Media

WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships - all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open - we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. 

WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.

For more information, visit wppmedia.com .

Role Summary & Impact

As a Senior Associate, Analytics, you will play a critical role in supporting Church & Dwight, a diverse CPG client and a stable WPP partner. You will be the analytical backbone for a portfolio of iconic brands (including ARM & HAMMER, OxiClean, Trojan, and Batiste), ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of media performance reporting across social, programmatic, digital, and e-commerce channels.

Your primary responsibility will be to manage and produce three large-scale brand reports simultaneously each month. This involves hands-on data cleansing, quality assurance, and collaborating closely with multiple internal investment teams to deliver actionable insights. This position offers a fantastic opportunity to develop robust project management skills, gain deep cross-channel analytics experience, and grow within a large, supportive analytics team.

Key Responsibilities

• Reporting & Analytics

• Simultaneously manage and produce 3 large monthly brand reports, creating campaign wrap-up analyses and performance summaries.

• Aggregate and analyze large datasets from multiple media channels, including social, programmatic, digital investment, and e-commerce (search and display).

• Utilize advanced Excel functions to manipulate data, create pivot tables, and generate insights for reporting.

• Data Quality Assurance (QA) & Cleansing

• Conduct rigorous and detail-oriented QA on campaign data, including taxonomy and benchmark validation.

• Identify, troubleshoot, and flag data discrepancies (e.g., incorrect placement names, tracking issues) to the respective investment teams for correction.

• Perform data cleansing and validation to ensure the highest level of accuracy before data is used in client-facing reports.

• Project & Stakeholder Management

• Act as a project manager for your reporting deliverables, coordinating staggered timelines and managing internal due dates across multiple teams.

• Serve as a key point of contact for internal investment teams, communicating data needs and QA findings effectively.

• Organize and maintain project schedules to ensure timely delivery of reports for internal reviews and client presentations.

Qualifications:

• Experience:  1-3 years of relevant work experience in media analytics, data analysis, or a related role, ideally within a media agency.

• Advanced Excel Proficiency (Critical):  Mastery of Excel, including pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, IF/THEN statements, and the ability to manage and analyze large, complex datasets.

• Data QA & Attention to Detail:  A highly detail-oriented mindset with proven experience in data cleansing, validation, and quality assurance processes (e.g., taxonomy QA).

• Project Management Skills:  Strong organizational and time-management skills with the demonstrated ability to manage multiple simultaneous projects and deadlines.

• Cross-Channel Knowledge:  Familiarity with reporting and metrics across various media channels (e.g., social, programmatic, search, display).

Communication Skills:  Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with multiple internal teams.

description:
What We're Researching
We're running a paid study on supplier invoice processing and tax compliance workflows. Managing exceptions, such as missing tax documentation, is a critical part of financial operations. We want to understand how finance teams evaluate these edge cases to decide whether a bill should be paid, rejected, or investigated further.
How It Works
During a remote AI-moderated interview, you will review a simulated accounts payable scenario involving a supplier bill. title: Research Engineer, Takeoff Intel
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the team

At Anthropic, we are delegating a growing share of AI development to AI systems themselves . Takeoff Intel is the team that measures this recursion from the inside. We're part of the Anthropic Institute . We design evaluations of AI R&D capabilities, build the internal telemetry Anthropic uses to track how much of its own model development is becoming AI-assisted, and develop the quantitative methods that turn those signals into a calibrated picture of where capability growth is heading, so that Anthropic and the wider world have accurate situational awareness on this acceleration.

Our work appears in Anthropic's model system cards (we own the AI R&D capability assessments and adapted Epoch's Capabilities Index to our evals); all the data in When AI Builds Itself comes from our team. Internally, our measurements shape research priorities and safety planning; externally, they contribute to Anthropic's public reporting on the pace of AI progress and to collaborations with third-party evaluators. We're a small team that works closely with pretraining, RL, economics, and policy researchers across the company. If you're passionate about measurement accuracy, and feel urgency about safety and situational awareness, you should consider joining us.

 

About the role

As a Research Engineer on Takeoff Intel you'll build and run the evaluation and measurement instruments that make this research possible. This is a generalist role on a small team: you'll work across evals infrastructure, large-scale data processing, and analysis tooling, and you'll prioritize shipping. We build instruments that answer real questions and help set priorities, not dashboards that surface noise. We value working prototypes, rapid iteration, accuracy and good prioritization. We often need to go from a vague research question to a running instrument quickly.

We're hiring at both junior and senior levels.

Responsibilities

•
Design, build, and run capability evaluations and measurement instruments at scale

•
Build the data and analysis pipelines that turn large volumes of model outputs and telemetry into reliable metrics

•
Prototype new instruments fast, validate them, and decide what to keep

•
Review and supervise AI-written code as a normal part of the workflow

•
Work closely with research scientists on the team and with partner teams to define what's worth measuring

•
Contribute to internal write-ups and public reporting

You may be a good fit if you

•
Have shipped an evaluation, data product, or research library end to end

•
Prototype fast and are comfortable throwing code away

•
Handle messy, large-volume data without over-engineering

•
Have run experiments on large language models, not just moved their outputs around

•
Can work from a vague question rather than a spec

•
Communicate results clearly and collaborate closely with the researchers whose questions your instruments answer

Strong candidates may also have

•
Built evaluation harnesses or benchmark infrastructure for LLMs

•
Experience with large-scale ML or data infrastructure (self-driving, observability, or similar) alongside ML exposure

•
Built tools or libraries that other researchers rely on

•
A track record of catching what AI-written code gets wrong

 

Some examples of our work

•
Anthropic ECI:  our adaptation of Epoch Capabilities Index published in all recent system cards to measure capability acceleration

•
AI R&D capability assessments in the Claude system cards

description:

Staff Engineer, Applied AI (Customer Agent)

About the Team:

Our Engineering team builds the AI systems that power how brands run their businesses on Klaviyo. We move fast, ship in production, and hold a high bar for what "AI-native" actually means: systems that make real judgment calls, not demos.

The Customer Agent team is one of the newest and most ambitious groups in that org, based in Boston and working in-office: we're building a conversational AI system that lets brands serve their own customers at a scale no human support team could match. We're still small enough that one engineer’s work visibly shapes how the whole platform evolves. We're past the demo stage: the team ships changes against live customer traffic, measures quality with real evaluation frameworks, and treats reliability as a product feature, not an afterthought.

About the Role:

As a Staff Engineer, you'll set the technical and product direction for a core area of Customer Agent end to end, building a 0-to-1 agentic product with the speed and ownership of a startup, backed by the scale and resources of one of the most innovative tech companies on the East Coast, while staying hands-on with the hardest problems yourself. This is a lead-level role, with a wide footprint across our agentic product - from orchestration to governance - that grows based on where the product is when you join. We're looking for an engineer who owns complex, ambiguous problems, who has built, scaled, and supported a production agentic system through everything that comes after the demo, and who up-levels the people, process, and technology around them.

How You'll Make an Impact:

• Set the technical and product direction for a core area of Customer Agent, from architecture through production, and contribute to the direction of the platform overall.

• Take on the hardest technical problems in your area: orchestration, evaluation, guardrails, memory & context, failure handling for non-deterministic systems.

• Write and ship code, review designs, and make the hard calls in your area when there’s no obvious right answer.

• Define patterns that other engineers adopt, and mentor through design reviews rather than direct management.

• Partner with product, design, data science, and go-to-market leaders to shape what gets built, not just how it’s built.

• Evaluate emerging AI technologies and bring the ones worth betting on into production.

What We're Looking For:

• You've built, scaled, and supported production agentic systems, not just prototyped them: real orchestration, evals, guardrails, and non-deterministic failure handling. You've owned your part of one through launch, incidents, and the operational reality after the demo.

• You've learned the hard lessons that only come from running agents in production: securing them against misuse and abuse, and the operational scar tissue of keeping a non-deterministic system reliable as usage grows.

• You've owned technical and product direction for a significant area before, not just your own component, and you can point to something you designed and championed that shipped and that other engineers built on.

• You're hands-on: writing code, reviewing your own and others’ architecture decisions, and debugging production issues yourself, not delegating the hardest problems away.

• Your patterns and designs are reused by other engineers, and you've unblocked many others’ projects, not just your own.
